findings.title: getBaseConditions returns an un-parenthesized OR expression when there are no filters
findings.body:
When both auth and filter conditions exist, `getBaseConditions` wraps each one: `(auth) AND (filter)`. When there are no filters, it returns `authConditions` unwrapped. For org and team scope that is `(teamBranch) OR (userBranch)`.

The old `findMany` let Prisma's `AND` array handle grouping. Raw-SQL callers will now write things like `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`. Because SQL `AND` binds tighter than `OR`, that becomes `teamBranch OR (userBranch AND createdAt >= ...)`. Every caller-supplied predicate (date range, status, etc.) is then silently ignored for all team bookings.

The same problem affects the public `getFilterConditions`, which returns the bare `"eventTypeId" = X OR "eventParentId" = X`. Combining it as `${auth} AND ${filter}` would match any row with `eventParentId = X`, including rows outside the authorized set.

Fix: wrap every returned fragment in parentheses, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions})\``, or build each OR fragment already wrapped.

findings.title: Dead fallback branch would return filter conditions without any authorization
findings.body:
`getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. So the `else if (filterConditions) return filterConditions` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches can never run.

The branch is also dangerous as written. If auth conditions ever become nullable or empty in a refactor, the method would return only the user-supplied filters with no authorization restriction, exposing bookings across tenants.

The fallback for a missing auth condition should be `NOTHING_CONDITION`, never the filter alone, or the dead branches should be removed.

findings.title: Public findMany method removed without a replacement query method
findings.body:
`findMany(findManyArgs)` was the service's public query entry point. It is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment.

Any existing or in-flight caller of `insightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will stop compiling. Each caller now has to hand-write `$queryRaw` against `"BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"` and get operator precedence right itself (see the parenthesization issue).

The PR description presents this as a test-only update and does not mention the API removal.

findings.title: Org/team SQL fragments are never executed against the database
findings.body:
The only test that runs a generated condition against Postgres uses user scope (`"userId" = X AND "teamId" IS NULL`).

The org and team fragments use hand-written raw SQL: `"teamId" = ANY(${array})` with JS arrays as parameters, and the `"isTeamBooking"` column. Tests only compare them structurally against identical template literals. A wrong column name, an array/type mismatch in `ANY(...)`, or a precedence bug (e.g. appending `AND ...` to an OR expression) would pass these tests.

The PR description also says the tests could not be run locally. A `$queryRaw` assertion for org and team scope would actually validate the new SQL.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted although caching logic remains
findings.body:
The `Caching` describe block, which covered `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` caching, was removed outright instead of being ported to the `Prisma.sql` format.

The service still caches via `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions`, including the `null`-vs-`undefined` distinction for filters. A regression there (e.g. re-querying memberships on every call, or treating a cached `null` as uncached) is now untested.
